subject: Modular surge credit & feature bindings — packaging options for Clearline pilot
messages:
From: Avery Miller <avery@clearline.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 20 May 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Packaging question: pilot -> production economics

Hi Ben,

Thanks again for the demo last week — the latency profile looked promising. I attached our rough usage estimates (clearline_usage_estimates.xlsx) so you can see expected token volumes and burst patterns.

Two quick asks as we think about moving the pilot to prod in Q3:
- We need guidance on seat-based (Compact) vs throughput-based (Dedicated/Throughput) packaging for our mixed workloads (lots of short queries, occasional large-batch analytics).
- Can Redwood support an initial surge credit or burst allowance for the first 90 days? We expect a ramp where concurrent requests spike ~3x for short windows and we want to avoid throttling while we tune caching.

Also, we need clarity on which paid features would be considered part of the base package vs add-ons — structured output (JSON schema enforcement) and server-side reranking are high priority for us.

Can you outline a recommended path and ballpark economics? Procurement will need a draft with clear rollback/exit terms.

Appreciate it,
Avery
Senior PM, Platform
Clearline Health
From: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>
To: Avery Miller <avery@clearline.com>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 20 May 2028 10:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Packaging question: pilot -> production economics

Hi Avery — great to hear. I reviewed the estimates you sent. Quick replies inline and a short set of options below. I attached a one-page plan matrix (redwood-plan-matrix-v1.pdf).

Pattern questions (so my recommendation is tuned):
- Typical concurrency per endpoint during spike windows? (peak concurrent requests)
- Percent of traffic that is long-sequence (analytics) vs short queries?
- Regional restriction (US only or multi-region)?

High-level options:
1) Compact (seat-based) — best for spiky low-token workloads where each seat gives predictable concurrency; lower RTT variance but can cost more if you have sustained high token throughput.
2) Throughput (reserved capacity + token-metering) — better unit economics for sustained token-heavy batch jobs; plus we can add burst credits for short spikes.
3) Hybrid (reserved pool + elastic burst) — reserved baseline for the steady state and a burst credit bucket that auto-applies for short windows.

Credits: I can offer a one-time 20% surge credit on committed capacity for the first 90 days as a standard Sales concession; anything above that needs mgmt approval.

Feature bundling: structured output support and the server-side reranker are typically add-ons on small pilots, but we can include Structured Output in the pilot at no extra charge if you commit to a 12-month term on reserved capacity. Reranking would remain an add-on but we can discount it for the first year.

Next steps: if you confirm concurrency and region I can draft a pricing amendment and route a 20% surge credit approval.

Ben
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
From: Avery Miller <avery@clearline.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>
Cc: procurement@clearline.com
Date: Tue, 21 May 2028 08:30:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Packaging question: pilot -> production economics

Ben — thanks, that clarifies a lot. Answers:
- Peak concurrency ~150 requests for the UI endpoints, burst windows last ~2–4 minutes, expected ~10 such windows/day during ramp.
- Traffic split ~80% short queries, 20% long analytics.
- US-only for now.

Procurement has two asks before we can sign:
1) Can the surge credit be 25% instead of 20% for first 90 days? That helps our internal cost projections.
2) We need structured output and server-side reranking included for at least 12 months as part of the committed package — procurement is pushing back on line-item add-ons during the first year.

Also: What does rollback look like if we undercommit? We prefer a prorated exit with a 60-day notice window. I attached procurement_reqs.pdf with detail.

Avery
From: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>
To: Lauren Bishop <lauren@redwood.ai>, Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 22 May 2028 14:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Fwd: Packaging question: pilot -> production economics (Clearline) — approval request

Looping you in — summary and ask:
- Clearline (DEAL-9931) wants a 25% surge credit for first 90 days (we originally offered 20%).
- They also want Structured Output and server-side reranking bundled into the committed package for 12 months (no line-item charge year 1).
- Their usage: ~150 concurrent peaks, US-only, 80/20 short/long split.
- They prefer a prorated exit with 60-day notice if they undercommit.

My recommended counter: approve 25% surge credit for 90 days (to close) but require a 12-month minimum committed reservation at the agreed committed throughput. Offer Structured Output included for 12 months, but make server-side reranking a discounted add-on (40% off year 1) instead of fully waived. Keep the 60-day prorated exit but add a cap on usage overage to avoid open-ended cost.

If you approve I will: 1) send an amendment draft (pricing_amendment_draft.docx), 2) prepare a short one-page legal summary for procurement, 3) request pricing sign-off and set up a kickoff.

Thoughts?

Thanks,
Ben
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
